response.sql: WITH g AS (SELECT s.riskeval AS riskeval, AVG(sc.gbsize / sc.spanmin) AS rate FROM scans sc JOIN sites s ON s.zoneregistry = sc.zoneref WHERE sc.gbsize / sc.spanmin IS NOT NULL GROUP BY s.riskeval), b AS (SELECT AVG(rate) AS bm FROM g) SELECT AVG(g.rate) AS avg_rate_above_benchmark, AVG(g.rate - b.bm) AS avg_excess_over_benchmark FROM g, b WHERE g.rate > b.bm

assumptions.assumption: A site with no recorded risk evaluation status means riskeval IS NULL. GROUP BY puts all NULLs in one group, so they form their own group. Empty strings, if any, would be a separate group.
A scan with spanmin = 0 gives a NULL ratio in SQLite, so it is ignored like any other missing ratio. A group with no valid ratios has no rate, so it is left out of the benchmark and the result.
If no group is above the benchmark, the query returns one row with NULLs in both columns.
